title: The Hot day in August
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：hot　|　正文 333 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 hot 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the foreman wrote of ① a hot day in August in the sheet, and everybody in the site said at once that it was ② hotter than the one named there the year before. Three shifts on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the foreman, who never explained anything, had done it in public and gone home; it was the hot ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the hottest day in August anybody in the site had ever seen, or so the sheet for May 1943 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too hot to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the worker who had come to help; the hot ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the rope at the far ramp, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a hot soup from the pot, and said that no worker in his right mind would call it ⑥ as hot as the soup from the pot they had once had in the old site. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was hot or not, and he said so.

By 1956 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the sheet. What the line asked for was ⑦ something hot, and nothing besides. The worker from the next site called the whole plan ⑧ quite hot; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the sheet kept the names of the hot ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1959, in silence, she wrote of another hot day in August in the same sheet, and the work, which took two shifts, seemed ⑨ hotter than anybody had expected. ⑩ The hottest soup from the pot in the whole site, she said in 1961, was the one she could never quite name; the hot ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 炎热（前置定语 a hot day in August：1949 年工头在施工单里记下的那件炎热的一天）
B. adj. 炎热／辛辣（比较级 hotter than：文中两处，一处比八月里炎热的一天，一处比预想）
C. adj. 炎热／辛辣（最高级 the hottest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 炎热（表语 too hot to do：母亲觉得它太炎热，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 辛辣（前置定语 a hot soup from the pot：叔叔把整件事称作一桩辛辣的汤）
F. adj. 辛辣（同级比较 as hot as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩锅里辛辣的汤相比）
G. adj. 辛辣（后置定语 something hot：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 辛辣（受程度副词修饰 quite hot：那位工人的评价）

items.q: the hottest day in August anybody
a hot soup from the pot
The hottest soup from the pot in

answers.why: hot 意为“炎热”，1949 年工头在施工单里记下的是“一件炎热的一天”，此处作前置定语 a hot day in August。
hot 意为“炎热”，此处用比较级 hotter than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
hot 意为“炎热”，施工单上 五月 那行字说它是工地里最炎热的一件，故用最高级 the hottest day in August。
hot 意为“炎热”，母亲认为这件东西“太炎热了，谁也用不上”，too hot to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
hot 意为“辛辣”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩辛辣的汤”，此处作前置定语 a hot soup from the pot。
hot 意为“辛辣”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩锅里辛辣的汤一样辛辣”，同级比较用 as hot as。
hot 意为“辛辣”，施工单上那半行字要的是“辛辣的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something hot。
hot 意为“辛辣”，邻工地来的那位工人认为这套计划“相当辛辣”，quite 修饰原级 hot。
hot 意为“辛辣”，1959 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要辛辣”，故用比较级 hotter than。
hot 意为“辛辣”，母亲 1961 年说的是“整个工地里最辛辣的那一桩”，故用最高级 the hottest soup from the pot。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1949 年，工头在施工单里记下了一件炎热的一天。（a hot day in August）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更炎热。（hotter than …）
母亲觉得它太炎热，谁也用不上。（too hot to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩辛辣的汤。（a hot soup from the pot）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩锅里辛辣的汤一样辛辣。（as hot as …）
到了 1956 年，施工单上只剩半行字：要的是一件辛辣的东西。（something hot）
answers: In 1949 the foreman wrote of a hot day in August in the sheet.
Everybody said it was hotter than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too hot to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a hot soup from the pot.
He said nobody would call it as hot as the soup from the pot they had once had.
By 1956 the sheet asked for nothing but something hot.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 hot 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1949 the foreman wrote of a hot day in August in the sheet, and nobody forgot it.
It was the hottest day in August in the site, or so the sheet says.
My mother thought it too hot to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a hot soup from the pot, and nobody argued with him.
The worker from the next site called the plan quite hot, and everybody laughed.
The hot ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
